answer.generated: Auxiliary memory serves as an extension to main memory by storing program and data files, typically visible to the programmer through the abstraction of files and records rather than individual bytes or words. This extension is particularly important for providing additional storage capacity beyond what is physically available in main memory. The concept of virtual memory leverages auxiliary memory to create the illusion of a much larger contiguous address space for processes, thereby enhancing the efficiency and performance of the system by dynamically managing the mapping between logical addresses and physical locations across both main and auxiliary memory.
